recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: For a plane lamina, the sum of the
moments of inertia about two mutually
perpendicular axes in its plane equals
the moment of inertia about the axis
steps.why: The 2-mark form of the 4-mark theorem SAQ — the statement is the same words either way.
common_mistakes: Forgetting "plane lamina" — the theorem is for flat bodies only.

recall.must_convey: That for a plane lamina, the two in-plane perpendicular axes sum to the normal axis.
accept: two perpendicular axes in the plane
reject: parallel axis through the centre of mass

steps.memory_tip: Two axes IN the plane add up to the one PERPENDICULAR to it. Flat bodies only.
steps.margin_note: First mark. "Plane lamina" and "point of intersection" are both marked words.

steps.label: The equation
steps.why: Three symbols; the lamina condition does the rest.
common_mistakes: Writing I_x = I_y + I_z with the roles scrambled.

accept: I z equals I x plus I y
reject: I equals I naught plus M r squared

steps.memory_tip: z is the axis out of the plane, so I_z is the one by itself: I_z = I_x + I_y.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One line, and say which axis z is.

insider_note: Name the axes as you write I_z = I_x + I_y — an unlabelled equation is not the theorem, and it is half the marks here.
